Package com.nexuslink.protocol.db

Class MavenCommandHelp

java.lang.Object
com.nexuslink.protocol.db.MavenCommandHelp
public final class MavenCommandHelp extends Object
Generates the mvn command a user should run in their own terminal to fetch a JDBC driver jar, per shell.

Why hand the user a command instead of just downloading it

In a locked-down organisation the machine's Maven is already configured correctly — the internal Artifactory mirror, the credentials, the proxy, the corporate CA — in ~/.m2/settings.xml and the developer's shell environment. Reproducing all of that inside the app is guesswork that fails in exactly the environments that need it most. ExternalDriverLoader still tries the direct download because it works for many users, but when it can't, running one mvn command in a shell that is already known to work is the reliable path: Maven resolves the jar through the org's own mirror, and the user then attaches the resulting file.

dependency:copy is used rather than plain dependency:get because it also places the jar in a known output directory, so the user has a concrete file to point at.
